analysis:
This batch changes only tests. StatusCommandRunTests.swift adds lateLeaseRenewalStillAuthorizes at head lines 253-279. ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests.swift adds head tests at lines 100-271 and migrates summary() to a new removalAuthorization parameter.

The tests specify the new production behavior:
- displayedProviderAuthorization/displayedStatus shows App Attest authorization for an unexpired lease whose renewal is older than snapshotMaxAge (receivedAt 85, expiresAt 115).
- currentProviderAuthorization/currentStatus, which gates MDM removal/unenroll, still requires receipt within the window. receivedAt 89.999 yields nil.
- summary offers 'removal is available'/'unenroll' only when the removal decision exists and matches the displayed grant's session, machine, reason, protocolVersion and mdmRemovalReady. Otherwise it says 'needs fresh coordinator readiness' and to keep profiles installed.
- Display requires process identity, coordinator URL match and online status, and fails closed on expired, NaN or infinite expiry. It is also bounded by writtenAt freshness (102.001 and 110.001 are rejected).

This matters for T-057, premature MDM removal, and T-053/A-016, stale authorization. Removal stays fail-closed on late renewals, and display is local CLI diagnostic only, not serving permission (T-052).

No regression is identified in the test code. However, the production implementation is not supplied: DaemonState.displayedProviderAuthorization, ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.displayedStatus/summary/removalReady, and the Status and doctor callers. Integration must verify that:
- no unenroll/MDM-removal path consumes displayedProviderAuthorization instead of currentProviderAuthorization;
- summary's matching of removalAuthorization against the displayed grant is enforced in production, not just in tests;
- the display window cannot outlive the daemon snapshot (writtenAt bound) or the expiresAt lease.

The threat-model text for T-057/TB-011 may need a note distinguishing display freshness from removal freshness.
